generic_desktop_gui.independence: Kitty, Slack, Tabiew and the required font do not depend on apps.enable, desktop.niri.enable or AI/work flags. Linux-only GUI utilities share the desktop.enable boundary. Existing private macOS Capacities, Zed and Paneru selections are not duplicated.

linux.providers: Official current Kitty bundle, Slack native deb without vendor repository activation, Tabiew native CLI, Capacities native deb and Canonical Chromium snap assertions; Noble-security Nautilus/wdisplays/grim/slurp.
linux.policy: No obsolete NixGL runtime or cross-release ABI mixing; system file-manager/display/screenshot backends retain their explicit distro-security exception and reason.

macos.providers: Homebrew cask kitty/slack/font-jetbrains-mono-nerd-font and formula tabiew, native arm64 only; font cask is the sole Mac JetBrainsMono Nerd Font owner.
macos.lifecycle: Ordinary Homebrew app/font registration and staging, no Nix Apps links or custom installer. Read-only payload/version/architecture/font-family checks bind ownership. Foreign and preexisting apps are preserved; ordinary non-zap retirement preserves app data. Historical Homebrew rollback is explicitly unavailable without retained exact artifacts; reviewed current reinstall is explicit provision.
macos.host_acceptance: Actual LaunchServices/login-session and OS consent acceptance remain separate unverified host gates; no startup install/update or automatic OS consent bypass.

shared_gui_dependencies.consumer: Public browsers/desktop and private native GUI app recipes share single Noble ABI package owners. Each app declares requires so independent flags do not silently lose runtime libraries.
shared_gui_dependencies.policy: Signed Noble security/ABI maintenance, not an upstream-latest graphics stack claim.
shared_gui_dependencies.retirement: These packages and base GTK/D-Bus/X11 ABI owners set retain_shared_runtime. Disabling apps/browser/desktop configuration removes no native ABI payload; explicit retirement records retained-shared-runtime rather than a false uninstalled result. libc, loader and other generic GUI dependencies follow the same policy in gui-linux.json.

native_desktop_dependencies.policy: Noble system libraries/security updates remain native and are not replaced with another Ubuntu release. Exact exceptional source/runtime pins and build/runtime closure are owned by desktop recipe manifests. Appearance has its own desktop/Nord predicates rather than inheriting compositor enable.

policy.native: Every active old package/function has a package owner or concrete configuration/recipe consumer.
policy.retired: Nix-only features are explicit removals, never disabled-default omissions.
policy.private: Listed responsibility remains in private entry point; no identity/secret/AI payload is copied here.
policy.apt: Signed Noble security/ABI exception, not upstream latest.
policy.brew: Concrete provider/version metadata; native updates compare upstream/provider/installed and do not claim immutable formula retention.
policy.shared_runtime_retirement: Base manifest retains Noble system Python/venv/pip, host OS command foundations, native Bash/Zsh login/rescue shells, Git and OS crypto/signing/SSH/bootstrap/verifier runtimes. Source/configuration/frontends may retire independently; retained native payload/provenance/services/data remain installed and recover reports no restore needed. This is not an uninstall claim or permission to purge/autoremove reverse dependencies.
policy.owned_application_retirement: Ordinary applications and optional tools remain removable when their recorded installed identity is unchanged. APT must simulate removal and permit exactly the requested owned package, ignoring only architecture qualifiers; empty/failed/foreign-cascade plans fail closed before escalation or mutation. No broad cleanup, dependency purge or implicit service/workload stop is authorized.
policy.mise: Exact canonical versions, platform lock; approved Go source tools use pinned toolchain and GoSumDB, npm uses package graph sidecars rather than invented artifact hashes.
policy.scope: Target actual Ubuntu24.04x86_64 and macOSarm64. Additional legacy lock platforms remain metadata, not qualified target claims.
